text:
emma: Quick planning thread: product wants a PRD + launch checklist for runtime changes (smart kernel routing, attention fast-path, KV retention controls). They've asked for clear pilot criteria and a customer pilot by end of next week.

li: A few questions up front: should smart kernel routing be model-agnostic or driven by per-model profiles? I lean per-model profiles to keep rollout safe.

rafael: agree per-model. Also propose we require deterministic kernel mapping for a given (model, seq_len, quantization_flag) so we can reproduce perf in customer reports.

emma: Good. Product note: NimbusPay requested strict billing stability and an opt-in for any cost-saving kernels. They will pilot if we guarantee p95 within 5% of baseline and no quality drift > 1%.

tina: Draft acceptance criteria from infra POV:
- Decision latency: routing decision <= 8ms per request.
- End-to-end p95 per-token latency <= 110ms on our 8k seq standard harness.
- Quality delta <= 1% measured on the nimbus-sim prompt set.
- Cost delta <= +12% for default mode; cost-saving kernels must be opt-in.

owen: Add observability requirements: tag each response with kernel_variant, routing_reason, kv_state (size_bytes), kv_eviction_count. Also emit a rollforward marker when we change kernel mid-session.

priya: Edge cases: session-level KV incompatibility when switching kernels mid-session. Decide rules: either keep KV opaque to kernel (runtime handles translation) or disallow mid-session switches for incompatible kernels. I recommend disallow for v1 and add a migration API in v2.

emma: Noted. Product prefers migration-on-switch but ok to defer to v2 if it's high risk. We'll document the limitation clearly.

li: Canary strategy suggestion: customer-level pilot (NimbusPay) + regional canary (us-west-2) for 5% traffic for 48 hours. Auto roll-back on breach: p99 latency > 300ms or quality regression > 1.5% over 15m.

rafael: Also require a manual gating checklist before canary: load test green, regression harness green, cost impact reviewed, and security sign-off.

tina: For KV retention: defaults: per-customer cap 200MB, per-session max 100k tokens, eviction policy LRU with optional pin API. Admins should be able to set per-customer override. Include metrics for pinned_count and eviction_by_policy.

owen: We'll need a migration runbook: steps to opt a customer into new routing, how to revert, and how to handle in-flight sessions. Draft one-liner runbook items in the PRD: enable flag -> run small pilot -> monitor -> increase -> full roll.

priya: Human evaluation: ML to run a 300-prompt customer simulation + 3 expert raters. Acceptance: average rubric delta < 0.4 and no catastrophic failures in top 5 prompts.

emma: Owners and deadlines I propose:
- RFC + PRD skeleton: li/rafael 0% draft by Tue COB
- Perf harness + queries: tina/owen by Wed
- ML regression + human eval plan: priya by Thu
- Security & billing wording: product/security (product to assign) by Thu

li: I'll start the RFC. Will include a short decision matrix for kernel selection: priority order = compatibility > quality_estimate > latency_estimate > cost.

rafael: Suggest we encode fallback policy: fallback to stable kernel if quality_drop > 1% OR p99 > 320ms sustained for 10m. Document thresholds in the PRD.

emma: Add launch checklist items: one-line acceptance lines for each metric (use this format):
ACCEPTANCE: [metric] <= [threshold] measured on [harness] over [window] with [traffic profile]

emma: Also need customer comms template and FAQ (what to expect, how to opt out). I'll draft and circulate.

infra-bot: infra-bot: RFC created by @li: https://rwd.redwood/rfcs/runtime-routing-kv-v2 status: draft

tina: I'll drop initial Grafana queries and example SQL for eviction metrics in the RFC comments.

priya: One more edge case: quantized kernels that change tokenization behavior slightly. Add a required tokenizer equivalence check and a note that any tokenizer shift requires explicit opt-in.

emma: Good catch. We'll require tokenizer parity test in regression harness.

li: Will tag owners in the RFC and link back here. If anyone has small TODOs, please add as comments in the RFC rather than here.

emma: Thanks all. Goal: pilot with NimbusPay next Friday. If something blocks, escalate in #eng-runtime. Closing thread.
